pages.text: The crafting grid can $(thing)average$() 2–8 compatible tobacco items. This is useful when the same tobacco has different quality values and will not stack naturally.

All inputs must be the same tobacco item and processing mode. Raw leaf can only average with the same raw leaf. Cured leaf must also have the same cure type. Single-variety loose tobacco must have the same cure and the same cut. Blended Tobacco is not quality-averaged this way because its component identity must remain intact.
pages.title: Compatibility Rules

pages.text: The result's quality is the arithmetic average of the participating crafting-grid slots, rounded to the nearest whole number. The output count equals the number of occupied tobacco slots. The recipe does not change the cure or cut of a compatible batch.
pages.title: Result

pages.text: Averaging combines compatible quality values. Tobacco Crates do something different: fill a full 3×3 grid with nine of the same tobacco item and the crate stores each unit losslessly, even when their NBT/components differ. Breaking the crate spills those exact nine inputs back out.
pages.title: Quality-Safe Consolidation
